In the app

A level project opens with guided mode on this chapter: the panel lists the tags the program needs (Make them), shows every rung below under its fold, checks that MainRoutine verifies, and ticks these results while you run the level:

  • Run mode, Start: the level completes (hopper empty, belt clear)
  • Every bottle in the right bin, none lost
  • Under par (230 s)

Hard · par 230 s

The job

The bulk filling line on its own, before Level 22 puts a lid press, a labeler and a code check after it: the silo of white paint, its two-stage outlet and fill lance, and the weighing conveyor under it, the infeed, the scale and the outfeed all on one VFD. Containers come down the feed in batches: 4 pails, 3 bag-in-boxes, 3 jugs, then 2 drums. Between batches the operator holds the feed until the line is clear and turns the FORMAT thumbwheel: 1 pail, 2 drum, 3 bag-in-box, 4 jug. Register each container on the encoder from Reg_PE (creep the last few pulses), stop it centred under the lance, tare it once it settles, put the lance in, fill fast then dribble, and lift the lance only once both valves are proved shut. Off centre the lance misses the opening and the paint goes over the side. Net targets, in tenths of a kg as the scale reads: pail and bag-in-box 240 (± 3), jug 48 (± 1), drum 2600 (± 20). Keep the silo topped up from Bulk_Supply. +100 for each container into Filled_Out at its weight, −100 for one shipped off weight or empty, −50 for each spill.

The program

The program is the classic silo’s, its routines one after another in MainRoutine: the first scan, the recipe from the thumbwheel, Start and Stop, the registration on the encoder with the creep, the tare and the two-stage fill with the lance held in until the valves are proved shut, the refill band, the count and the alarms.

The rungs

Watch for

Off centre the lance misses the opening. Register on the encoder from the eye and creep the last few pulses, so the container stops where the lance is.

Run it

Load the program, go to Run mode and leave the level to finish (press Start on its console where it has one). The score card shows how it went, and the guided checks above tick as each result happens. A run of this program on v2.02 completed in about 195 s against a par of 230 s, with 1400 points and nothing wrong.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: FIRST SCAN: nothing carried over from before the power blink. The count is kept

pred.q: S:FS is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: One_Done is unlatched, Reg_Active is unlatched, In_Place is unlatched, Fill_Done is unlatched, Tare_Taken is unlatched, Fill_Req is unlatched, Fill_Fault is unlatched, Valve_Fault is unlatched, Lance_Fault is unlatched, Format_Fault is unlatched, Motor_Fault is unlatched and LT_Fault is unlatched.

rungs.words: When S:FS is on, the rung unlatches One_Done (ONE mode: the container under the lance has filled; Start clears it), unlatches Reg_Active (A container is being registered: counting from the eye), unlatches In_Place (The container is centred under the lance; cleared when it leaves the prox), unlatches Fill_Done (The container under the lance is full; cleared when it leaves the prox), unlatches Tare_Taken (The tare is in for the container on the scale), unlatches Fill_Req (DEMAND mode: the FILL button pressed for the container under the lance), unlatches Fill_Fault (A container did not fill in time), unlatches Valve_Fault (An outlet valve did not do what it was told), unlatches Lance_Fault (The lance did not move), unlatches Format_Fault (The container on the scale weighs wrong for the format: the wrong container, or the wrong format set), unlatches Motor_Fault (The line's drive tripped (a motor overload) or is not ready) and unlatches LT_Fault (The level transmitter disagrees with the high-level switch).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(S:FS) Examine If Closed asks: true when S:FS is on.
  2. A branch of 12 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(One_Done) Output Unlatch does: unlatches One_Done. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Reg_Active) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Reg_Active. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(In_Place) Output Unlatch does: unlatches In_Place. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTU(Fill_Done) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fill_Done. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 5
    1. OTU(Tare_Taken) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Tare_Taken. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 6
    1. OTU(Fill_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fill_Req. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 7
    1. OTU(Fill_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fill_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 8
    1. OTU(Valve_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Valve_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 9
    1. OTU(Lance_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lance_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 10
    1. OTU(Format_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Format_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 11
    1. OTU(Motor_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Motor_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 12
    1. OTU(LT_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches LT_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears One_Done when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: FORMAT 1, THE 5-GALLON PAIL: 24.0 kg of paint net (about 18 litres of white latex at 1.32 kg a litre), the last 2.5 kg on the dribble valve. Every weight here is in tenths of a kg, as the scale reads
rungs.words: When Format (Format_TW Value: The digits read as one number) equals 1, the rung puts 240 into Target (Recipe: the net fill, tenths of a kg), puts 25 into Dribble (Recipe: the last part of the fill on the dribble valve alone, tenths of a kg), puts 2 into Preact (Recipe: what is still in the air when the dribble valve shuts, tenths of a kg), puts 6 into Tare_Lo (Recipe: the lightest empty container of the format, tenths of a kg), puts 15 into Tare_Hi (Recipe: the heaviest empty container of the format, tenths of a kg) and puts 30 into Stop_Count (Recipe: encoder pulses from the registration eye to the container centred under the lance).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Format,1) Equal asks: true when Format equals 1. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. A branch of 6 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(240,Target) Move does: puts 240 into Target. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(25,Dribble) Move does: puts 25 into Dribble. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. MOV(2,Preact) Move does: puts 2 into Preact. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 4
    1. MOV(6,Tare_Lo) Move does: puts 6 into Tare_Lo. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 5
    1. MOV(15,Tare_Hi) Move does: puts 15 into Tare_Hi. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 6
    1. MOV(30,Stop_Count) Move does: puts 30 into Stop_Count. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: FORMAT 2, THE 55-GALLON DRUM: 260.0 kg net (about 197 litres, headroom left in a 208-litre drum), the last 20 kg on the dribble.

pred.q: Format is 1. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Target is not written (it keeps its value), Dribble is not written (it keeps its value), Preact is not written (it keeps its value), Tare_Lo is not written (it keeps its value), Tare_Hi is not written (it keeps its value) and Stop_Count is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at EQU(Format,2).

rungs.words: When Format (Format_TW Value: The digits read as one number) equals 2, the rung puts 2600 into Target (Recipe: the net fill, tenths of a kg), puts 200 into Dribble (Recipe: the last part of the fill on the dribble valve alone, tenths of a kg), puts 5 into Preact (Recipe: what is still in the air when the dribble valve shuts, tenths of a kg), puts 150 into Tare_Lo (Recipe: the lightest empty container of the format, tenths of a kg), puts 220 into Tare_Hi (Recipe: the heaviest empty container of the format, tenths of a kg) and puts 33 into Stop_Count (Recipe: encoder pulses from the registration eye to the container centred under the lance).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Format,2) Equal asks: true when Format equals 2. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. A branch of 6 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(2600,Target) Move does: puts 2600 into Target. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(200,Dribble) Move does: puts 200 into Dribble. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. MOV(5,Preact) Move does: puts 5 into Preact. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 4
    1. MOV(150,Tare_Lo) Move does: puts 150 into Tare_Lo. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 5
    1. MOV(220,Tare_Hi) Move does: puts 220 into Tare_Hi. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 6
    1. MOV(33,Stop_Count) Move does: puts 33 into Stop_Count. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: FORMAT 3, THE 5-GALLON BAG-IN-BOX: 24.0 kg net into the bag through its fitment
rungs.words: When Format (Format_TW Value: The digits read as one number) equals 3, the rung puts 240 into Target (Recipe: the net fill, tenths of a kg), puts 25 into Dribble (Recipe: the last part of the fill on the dribble valve alone, tenths of a kg), puts 2 into Preact (Recipe: what is still in the air when the dribble valve shuts, tenths of a kg), puts 3 into Tare_Lo (Recipe: the lightest empty container of the format, tenths of a kg), puts 10 into Tare_Hi (Recipe: the heaviest empty container of the format, tenths of a kg) and puts 30 into Stop_Count (Recipe: encoder pulses from the registration eye to the container centred under the lance).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Format,3) Equal asks: true when Format equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. A branch of 6 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(240,Target) Move does: puts 240 into Target. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(25,Dribble) Move does: puts 25 into Dribble. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. MOV(2,Preact) Move does: puts 2 into Preact. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 4
    1. MOV(3,Tare_Lo) Move does: puts 3 into Tare_Lo. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 5
    1. MOV(10,Tare_Hi) Move does: puts 10 into Tare_Hi. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 6
    1. MOV(30,Stop_Count) Move does: puts 30 into Stop_Count. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: FORMAT 4, THE GALLON JUG: 4.8 kg net (a gallon of paint), all of it on the dribble valve (the dribble is the whole target, so the butterfly never opens): the bulk flow would put a gallon over before the valve could shut

pred.q: Format is 4. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Target is written, Dribble is written, Preact is written, Tare_Lo is written, Tare_Hi is written and Stop_Count is written.

rungs.words: When Format (Format_TW Value: The digits read as one number) equals 4, the rung puts 48 into Target (Recipe: the net fill, tenths of a kg), puts 48 into Dribble (Recipe: the last part of the fill on the dribble valve alone, tenths of a kg), puts 2 into Preact (Recipe: what is still in the air when the dribble valve shuts, tenths of a kg), puts 0 into Tare_Lo (Recipe: the lightest empty container of the format, tenths of a kg), puts 3 into Tare_Hi (Recipe: the heaviest empty container of the format, tenths of a kg) and puts 27 into Stop_Count (Recipe: encoder pulses from the registration eye to the container centred under the lance).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Format,4) Equal asks: true when Format equals 4. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. A branch of 6 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(48,Target) Move does: puts 48 into Target. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(48,Dribble) Move does: puts 48 into Dribble. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. MOV(2,Preact) Move does: puts 2 into Preact. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 4
    1. MOV(0,Tare_Lo) Move does: puts 0 into Tare_Lo. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 5
    1. MOV(3,Tare_Hi) Move does: puts 3 into Tare_Hi. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 6
    1. MOV(27,Stop_Count) Move does: puts 27 into Stop_Count. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: A format the recipe knows
rungs.words: When Format (Format_TW Value: The digits read as one number) is at least 1 and Format is at most 4, the rung turns Format_OK (The format on the thumbwheel is 1 to 4) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. GEQ(Format,1) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Format is at least 1.
  2. LEQ(Format,4) Less Than or Equal asks: true when Format is at most 4.
  3. OTE(Format_OK) Output Energize does: turns Format_OK on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: A moving value can step over any single number between two scans; a window catches it on the way through.
pats.think: meeting a train. You cannot stand at one exact inch of track and wait for it to stop there; you watch the whole platform.
pats.watch: An EQU on a measured value (a position, a level, a weight) may never be true: the value jumps from just under to just over between scans.

rungs.head: Rung 6
rungs.comment: THE CUT-OFFS: the butterfly shuts at Target − Dribble, the dribble valve at Target − Preact, so what is still falling makes up the target. The registration slows to a creep 15 pulses before the stop count. STOP COUNT is the encoder pulses (one every 2 px, 33 mm) from the registration eye catching the container's leading edge to its centre under the lance: the eye-to-lance distance plus half the container
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung makes Fast_Cut (Net weight where the butterfly valve shuts: Target − Dribble) = Target (Recipe: the net fill, tenths of a kg) − Dribble (Recipe: the last part of the fill on the dribble valve alone, tenths of a kg), makes Slow_Cut (Net weight where the dribble valve shuts: Target − Preact) = Target − Preact (Recipe: what is still in the air when the dribble valve shuts, tenths of a kg) and makes Slow_Count (Where the creep starts: Stop_Count − 15) = Stop_Count (Recipe: encoder pulses from the registration eye to the container centred under the lance) − 15.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. SUB(Target,Dribble,Fast_Cut) Subtract does: makes Fast_Cut = Target − Dribble. Every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. SUB(Target,Preact,Slow_Cut) Subtract does: makes Slow_Cut = Target − Preact. Every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. SUB(Stop_Count,15,Slow_Count) Subtract does: makes Slow_Count = Stop_Count − 15. Every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 7
rungs.comment: THE SYSTEM may run: the E-Stop healthy (its contact is normally closed: 1 while healthy) and no fault latched
rungs.words: When EStop_OK (EStop OK: NC contact: 1 while healthy, 0 when pressed) is on, Motor_Fault (The line's drive tripped (a motor overload) or is not ready) is off, Valve_Fault (An outlet valve did not do what it was told) is off, Lance_Fault (The lance did not move) is off, Fill_Fault (A container did not fill in time) is off and Format_Fault (The container on the scale weighs wrong for the format: the wrong container, or the wrong format set) is off, the rung turns Sys_OK (The line may run: the E-Stop healthy and no fault latched) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(EStop_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when EStop_OK is on.
  2. XIO(Motor_Fault) Examine If Open asks: true when Motor_Fault is off.
  3. XIO(Valve_Fault) Examine If Open asks: true when Valve_Fault is off.
  4. XIO(Lance_Fault) Examine If Open asks: true when Lance_Fault is off.
  5. XIO(Fill_Fault) Examine If Open asks: true when Fill_Fault is off.
  6. XIO(Format_Fault) Examine If Open asks: true when Format_Fault is off.
  7. OTE(Sys_OK) Output Energize does: turns Sys_OK on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: START clears the last ONE cycle…

pred.q: Start_PB_Pressed is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: One_Done is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Start_PB_Pressed).

rungs.words: When Start_PB_Pressed (Start_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed) is on, the rung unlatches One_Done (ONE mode: the container under the lance has filled; Start clears it).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Start_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB_Pressed is on.
  2. OTU(One_Done) Output Unlatch does: unlatches One_Done. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears One_Done when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.comment: …and starts the run, sealed in. STOP is a normally-closed button: 1 until pressed, so a broken wire stops the line the same as the button
rungs.words: When either (Start_PB_Pressed (Start_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed) is on) or (Run (The conveyors are running (Start, sealed in until Stop, a fault, or one container done in ONE)) is on), Stop_PB_Pressed (Stop_PB Pressed: NC contact: 1 until pressed) is on, Sys_OK (The line may run: the E-Stop healthy and no fault latched) is on and One_Done (ONE mode: the container under the lance has filled; Start clears it) is off, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB_Pressed is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(Stop_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Stop_PB_Pressed is on.
  3. XIC(Sys_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when Sys_OK is on.
  4. XIO(One_Done) Examine If Open asks: true when One_Done is off.
  5. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: ONE: a container filled ends the run; it waits under the lance, full, for the next Start
rungs.words: When Mode_Sel_Left (Mode_Sel Left: 1 in the left position) is on, Fill_Done (The container under the lance is full; cleared when it leaves the prox) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung latches One_Done (ONE mode: the container under the lance has filled; Start clears it) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Mode_Sel_Left) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mode_Sel_Left is on.
  2. XIC(Fill_Done) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_Done is on.
  3. ONS(One_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in One_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  4. OTL(One_Done) Output Latch does: latches One_Done on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: One_Done stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.comment: REGISTRATION: the retroreflective eye before the scale catches the container's leading edge as it breaks the beam (a diffuse eye would see a white drum sooner than a clear jug); the encoder count there is the start
rungs.words: When Reg_PE (Reg_PE Detect: Light beam interrupted) is on, this is the first scan of it, Reg_Active (A container is being registered: counting from the eye) is off and In_Place (The container is centred under the lance; cleared when it leaves the prox) is off, the rung puts Enc_Pulses (In_Conv Pulses: Encoder pulses since Run mode started (counts down in reverse, wraps as an INT)) into Reg_Start (The encoder count when the eye caught the container) and latches Reg_Active on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reg_PE) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reg_PE is on.
  2. ONS(Reg_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Reg_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. XIO(Reg_Active) Examine If Open asks: true when Reg_Active is off.
  4. XIO(In_Place) Examine If Open asks: true when In_Place is off.
  5. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(Enc_Pulses,Reg_Start) Move does: puts Enc_Pulses into Reg_Start. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Reg_Active) Output Latch does: latches Reg_Active on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Reg_Active stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 12
rungs.comment: How far it has gone since. The encoder's count is an INT and wraps at 32767: a negative travel is a wrap

pred.q: Reg_Active is on and Reg_Travel is -1. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Reg_Travel is written and Reg_Travel is written.

rungs.words: When Reg_Active (A container is being registered: counting from the eye) is on, each path is tested on its own: it makes Reg_Travel (Pulses since the eye caught it) = Enc_Pulses (In_Conv Pulses: Encoder pulses since Run mode started (counts down in reverse, wraps as an INT)) − Reg_Start (The encoder count when the eye caught the container); if Reg_Travel is less than 0, it makes Reg_Travel = Reg_Travel + 65536.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reg_Active) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reg_Active is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. SUB(Enc_Pulses,Reg_Start,Reg_Travel) Subtract does: makes Reg_Travel = Enc_Pulses − Reg_Start. Every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. LES(Reg_Travel,0) Less Than asks: true when Reg_Travel is less than 0.
    2. ADD(Reg_Travel,65536,Reg_Travel) Add does: makes Reg_Travel = Reg_Travel + 65536. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.comment: Fifteen pulses short of the stop, creep…
rungs.words: When Reg_Active (A container is being registered: counting from the eye) is on and Reg_Travel (Pulses since the eye caught it) is at least Slow_Count (Where the creep starts: Stop_Count − 15), the rung turns Creep (Near the stop: the line at a quarter speed) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reg_Active) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reg_Active is on.
  2. GEQ(Reg_Travel,Slow_Count) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Reg_Travel is at least Slow_Count.
  3. OTE(Creep) Output Energize does: turns Creep on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 14
rungs.comment: …and at the stop count it is centred under the lance

pred.q: Reg_Active is off, Reg_Travel is 45 and Stop_Count is 10. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: In_Place is left as it was and Reg_Active is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Reg_Active).

rungs.words: When Reg_Active (A container is being registered: counting from the eye) is on and Reg_Travel (Pulses since the eye caught it) is at least Stop_Count (Recipe: encoder pulses from the registration eye to the container centred under the lance), the rung latches In_Place (The container is centred under the lance; cleared when it leaves the prox) on and unlatches Reg_Active.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reg_Active) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reg_Active is on.
  2. GEQ(Reg_Travel,Stop_Count) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Reg_Travel is at least Stop_Count.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(In_Place) Output Latch does: latches In_Place on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Reg_Active) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Reg_Active. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: In_Place stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 15
rungs.comment: THE STATION: a container that has left the prox takes its place, its fill and its tare with it
rungs.words: When Cont_Prox (Cont_Prox Detect: Detecting: any solid part is within range) is off, the rung unlatches In_Place (The container is centred under the lance; cleared when it leaves the prox), unlatches Fill_Done (The container under the lance is full; cleared when it leaves the prox) and unlatches Tare_Taken (The tare is in for the container on the scale).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Cont_Prox) Examine If Open asks: true when Cont_Prox is off.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(In_Place) Output Unlatch does: unlatches In_Place. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Fill_Done) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fill_Done. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Tare_Taken) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Tare_Taken. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears In_Place when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 16
rungs.comment: A container in place that is not filled waits there

pred.q: In_Place is on and Fill_Done is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: At_Fill is on.

rungs.words: When In_Place (The container is centred under the lance; cleared when it leaves the prox) is on and Fill_Done (The container under the lance is full; cleared when it leaves the prox) is off, the rung turns At_Fill (A container is under the lance and has not been filled) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(In_Place) Examine If Closed asks: true when In_Place is on.
  2. XIO(Fill_Done) Examine If Open asks: true when Fill_Done is off.
  3. OTE(At_Fill) Output Energize does: turns At_Fill on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 17
rungs.comment: THE LINE — infeed, scale and outfeed on one VFD — runs while the run is on, no container is waiting to fill, the lance is up and both valves are proved shut. The drive's ramps start and stop it smoothly
rungs.words: When Run (The conveyors are running (Start, sealed in until Stop, a fault, or one container done in ONE)) is on, At_Fill (A container is under the lance and has not been filled) is off, Lance_Up (Silo LanceUp: Fill lance up (retracted) switch) is on, Valve_Closed (Silo ValveClosed: Both outlet valves proved shut (their closed switches in series)) is on and Sys_OK (The line may run: the E-Stop healthy and no fault latched) is on, the rung turns Line_VFD_Run (Line_VFD Run: Run while 1 (two-wire control)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(At_Fill) Examine If Open asks: true when At_Fill is off.
  3. XIC(Lance_Up) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lance_Up is on.
  4. XIC(Valve_Closed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Valve_Closed is on.
  5. XIC(Sys_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when Sys_OK is on.
  6. OTE(Line_VFD_Run) Output Energize does: turns Line_VFD_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 18
rungs.comment: THE SPEED: a quarter speed for the creep…

pred.q: Creep is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Line_VFD_SpeedRef is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at XIC(Creep).

rungs.words: When Creep (Near the stop: the line at a quarter speed) is on, the rung puts 2500 into Line_VFD_SpeedRef (Line_VFD SpeedRef: Speed reference: 0-10000 = 0-10.000 V = 0 to the 10 V frequency).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Creep) Examine If Closed asks: true when Creep is on.
  2. MOV(2500,Line_VFD_SpeedRef) Move does: puts 2500 into Line_VFD_SpeedRef. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 19
rungs.comment: …full speed (10.000 V) otherwise
rungs.words: When Creep (Near the stop: the line at a quarter speed) is off, the rung puts 10000 into Line_VFD_SpeedRef (Line_VFD SpeedRef: Speed reference: 0-10000 = 0-10.000 V = 0 to the 10 V frequency).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Creep) Examine If Open asks: true when Creep is off.
  2. MOV(10000,Line_VFD_SpeedRef) Move does: puts 10000 into Line_VFD_SpeedRef. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 20
rungs.comment: THE TARE: the container stops, the scale settles…

pred.q: At_Fill is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: T_Settle times toward its preset.

rungs.words: When At_Fill (A container is under the lance and has not been filled) is on, the rung runs the timer T_Settle (The scale settles after the container stops: 0.6 s) toward 600 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(At_Fill) Examine If Closed asks: true when At_Fill is on.
  2. TON(T_Settle,600,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_Settle toward 600 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_Settle counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 21
rungs.comment: …and the empty container is weighed, once
rungs.words: When T_Settle.DN (the done bit of T_Settle: The scale settles after the container stops: 0.6 s) is on and Tare_Taken (The tare is in for the container on the scale) is off, the rung puts Weight (Scale Weight: Weight on the scale, kg) into Tare (The empty container, weighed once it settles, tenths of a kg) and latches Tare_Taken on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_Settle.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_Settle.DN is on.
  2. XIO(Tare_Taken) Examine If Open asks: true when Tare_Taken is off.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(Weight,Tare) Move does: puts Weight into Tare. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Tare_Taken) Output Latch does: latches Tare_Taken on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Tare_Taken stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 22
rungs.comment: The tare in the format's window: the container on the scale is the one the format fills

pred.q: Tare_Taken is on, Tare is 31, Tare_Lo is 44 and Tare_Hi is 48. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Tare_OK is off. It stops at GEQ(Tare,Tare_Lo).

rungs.words: When Tare_Taken (The tare is in for the container on the scale) is on, Tare (The empty container, weighed once it settles, tenths of a kg) is at least Tare_Lo (Recipe: the lightest empty container of the format, tenths of a kg) and Tare is at most Tare_Hi (Recipe: the heaviest empty container of the format, tenths of a kg), the rung turns Tare_OK (The tare is in the format's window: the right container) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Tare_Taken) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tare_Taken is on.
  2. GEQ(Tare,Tare_Lo) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Tare is at least Tare_Lo.
  3. LEQ(Tare,Tare_Hi) Less Than or Equal asks: true when Tare is at most Tare_Hi.
  4. OTE(Tare_OK) Output Energize does: turns Tare_OK on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: A moving value can step over any single number between two scans; a window catches it on the way through.

rungs.head: Rung 23
rungs.comment: …if not, the wrong container (or the wrong format): stop before a drum gets a jug's fill or a jug a drum's
rungs.words: When Tare_Taken (The tare is in for the container on the scale) is on, Tare_OK (The tare is in the format's window: the right container) is off and Format_OK (The format on the thumbwheel is 1 to 4) is on, the rung latches Format_Fault (The container on the scale weighs wrong for the format: the wrong container, or the wrong format set) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Tare_Taken) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tare_Taken is on.
  2. XIO(Tare_OK) Examine If Open asks: true when Tare_OK is off.
  3. XIC(Format_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when Format_OK is on.
  4. OTL(Format_Fault) Output Latch does: latches Format_Fault on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Format_Fault stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 24
rungs.comment: NET: what has gone in

pred.q: Tare_Taken is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Net is written and Net_kg is written.

rungs.words: When Tare_Taken (The tare is in for the container on the scale) is on, the rung makes Net (What has gone into the container: Weight − Tare, tenths of a kg) = Weight (Scale Weight: Weight on the scale, kg) − Tare (The empty container, weighed once it settles, tenths of a kg) and makes Net_kg (Net, kg (for the display)) = Net ÷ 10.0.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Tare_Taken) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tare_Taken is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. SUB(Weight,Tare,Net) Subtract does: makes Net = Weight − Tare. Every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. DIV(Net,10.0,Net_kg) Divide does: makes Net_kg = Net ÷ 10.0.

rungs.head: Rung 25
rungs.comment: DEMAND: the FILL button asks for this container…
rungs.words: When Mode_Sel_Right (Mode_Sel Right: 1 in the right position) is on, At_Fill (A container is under the lance and has not been filled) is on and Fill_PB_Pressed (Fill_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed) is on, the rung latches Fill_Req (DEMAND mode: the FILL button pressed for the container under the lance) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Mode_Sel_Right) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mode_Sel_Right is on.
  2. XIC(At_Fill) Examine If Closed asks: true when At_Fill is on.
  3. XIC(Fill_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_PB_Pressed is on.
  4. OTL(Fill_Req) Output Latch does: latches Fill_Req on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Fill_Req stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 26
rungs.comment: …and the request goes with it

pred.q: At_Fill is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Fill_Req is left as it was. It stops at XIO(At_Fill).

rungs.words: When At_Fill (A container is under the lance and has not been filled) is off, the rung unlatches Fill_Req (DEMAND mode: the FILL button pressed for the container under the lance).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(At_Fill) Examine If Open asks: true when At_Fill is off.
  2. OTU(Fill_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fill_Req. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Fill_Req when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 27
rungs.comment: THE FILL is on for a weighed container of the right format, with product in the tank; in DEMAND only once FILL is pressed
rungs.words: When Run (The conveyors are running (Start, sealed in until Stop, a fault, or one container done in ONE)) is on, At_Fill (A container is under the lance and has not been filled) is on, Tare_Taken (The tare is in for the container on the scale) is on, Tare_OK (The tare is in the format's window: the right container) is on, Format_OK (The format on the thumbwheel is 1 to 4) is on, Silo_Low (The tank is low: under 10 %, until it is back over 20 %. No new fill starts) is off, either (Mode_Sel_Right (Mode_Sel Right: 1 in the right position) is off) or (Fill_Req (DEMAND mode: the FILL button pressed for the container under the lance) is on) and Sys_OK (The line may run: the E-Stop healthy and no fault latched) is on, the rung turns Fill_Go (The fill is on for the container under the lance) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(At_Fill) Examine If Closed asks: true when At_Fill is on.
  3. XIC(Tare_Taken) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tare_Taken is on.
  4. XIC(Tare_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tare_OK is on.
  5. XIC(Format_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when Format_OK is on.
  6. XIO(Silo_Low) Examine If Open asks: true when Silo_Low is off.
  7. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIO(Mode_Sel_Right) Examine If Open asks: true when Mode_Sel_Right is off.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Fill_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_Req is on.
  8. XIC(Sys_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when Sys_OK is on.
  9. OTE(Fill_Go) Output Energize does: turns Fill_Go on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 28
rungs.comment: The lance goes down into it and stays in until the fill is done and both valves are proved shut, so the last drops go into the container

pred.q: Fill_Go is on, Cont_Prox is on, Tare_Taken is on and Valve_Closed is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Lance_Down is on.

rungs.words: When either (Fill_Go (The fill is on for the container under the lance) is on) or (Cont_Prox (Cont_Prox Detect: Detecting: any solid part is within range) is on, Tare_Taken (The tare is in for the container on the scale) is on and Valve_Closed (Silo ValveClosed: Both outlet valves proved shut (their closed switches in series)) is off), the rung turns Lance_Down (Silo Lance: Fill lance air cylinder: down while on) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Fill_Go) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_Go is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Cont_Prox) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cont_Prox is on.
    2. XIC(Tare_Taken) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tare_Taken is on.
    3. XIO(Valve_Closed) Examine If Open asks: true when Valve_Closed is off.
  2. OTE(Lance_Down) Output Energize does: turns Lance_Down on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 29
rungs.comment: …a second for it to reach the bottom of its travel
rungs.words: When Fill_Go (The fill is on for the container under the lance) is on and Lance_Up (Silo LanceUp: Fill lance up (retracted) switch) is off, the rung runs the timer T_LanceIn (The lance's travel down into the container: 1.0 s) toward 1000 ms (1 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Fill_Go) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_Go is on.
  2. XIO(Lance_Up) Examine If Open asks: true when Lance_Up is off.
  3. TON(T_LanceIn,1000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_LanceIn toward 1000 ms (1 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_LanceIn counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Rung 30
rungs.comment: THE BULK: the butterfly valve open to Target − Dribble

pred.q: Fill_Go is off, T_LanceIn.DN is off, Net is 12 and Fast_Cut is 40. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Valve_Fast is off. It stops at XIC(Fill_Go).

rungs.words: When Fill_Go (The fill is on for the container under the lance) is on, T_LanceIn.DN (the done bit of T_LanceIn: The lance's travel down into the container: 1.0 s) is on and Net (What has gone into the container: Weight − Tare, tenths of a kg) is less than Fast_Cut (Net weight where the butterfly valve shuts: Target − Dribble), the rung turns Valve_Fast (Silo FillFast: Butterfly valve (bulk fill): open while on) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Fill_Go) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_Go is on.
  2. XIC(T_LanceIn.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_LanceIn.DN is on.
  3. LES(Net,Fast_Cut) Less Than asks: true when Net is less than Fast_Cut.
  4. OTE(Valve_Fast) Output Energize does: turns Valve_Fast on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 31
rungs.comment: THE DRIBBLE: the small valve open all the way to Target − Preact, alone at the end, so the cut-off is fine
rungs.words: When Fill_Go (The fill is on for the container under the lance) is on, T_LanceIn.DN (the done bit of T_LanceIn: The lance's travel down into the container: 1.0 s) is on and Net (What has gone into the container: Weight − Tare, tenths of a kg) is less than Slow_Cut (Net weight where the dribble valve shuts: Target − Preact), the rung turns Valve_Slow (Silo FillSlow: Dribble valve on the bypass: open while on) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Fill_Go) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_Go is on.
  2. XIC(T_LanceIn.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_LanceIn.DN is on.
  3. LES(Net,Slow_Cut) Less Than asks: true when Net is less than Slow_Cut.
  4. OTE(Valve_Slow) Output Energize does: turns Valve_Slow on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 32
rungs.comment: DONE: the lance comes up, and the line goes once it is up and the valves are shut

pred.q: Fill_Go is on, T_LanceIn.DN is on, Net is 17 and Slow_Cut is 12. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Fill_Done latches on.

rungs.words: When Fill_Go (The fill is on for the container under the lance) is on, T_LanceIn.DN (the done bit of T_LanceIn: The lance's travel down into the container: 1.0 s) is on and Net (What has gone into the container: Weight − Tare, tenths of a kg) is at least Slow_Cut (Net weight where the dribble valve shuts: Target − Preact), the rung latches Fill_Done (The container under the lance is full; cleared when it leaves the prox) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Fill_Go) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_Go is on.
  2. XIC(T_LanceIn.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_LanceIn.DN is on.
  3. GEQ(Net,Slow_Cut) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Net is at least Slow_Cut.

pats.why: Fill_Done stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Fill_Go) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_Go is on.
  2. XIC(T_LanceIn.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_LanceIn.DN is on.

rungs.comment: THE VALVE FEEDBACK: told shut and not proved shut, or the butterfly told open and still proved shut, for a second and a half
rungs.words: When either (Valve_Fast (Silo FillFast: Butterfly valve (bulk fill): open while on) is off, Valve_Slow (Silo FillSlow: Dribble valve on the bypass: open while on) is off and Valve_Closed (Silo ValveClosed: Both outlet valves proved shut (their closed switches in series)) is off) or (Valve_Fast is on and Valve_Closed is on), the rung runs the timer T_ValveFb (Valve feedback: the closed switches disagree with the outputs for 1.5 s) toward 1500 ms (1.5 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIO(Valve_Fast) Examine If Open asks: true when Valve_Fast is off.
    2. XIO(Valve_Slow) Examine If Open asks: true when Valve_Slow is off.
    3. XIO(Valve_Closed) Examine If Open asks: true when Valve_Closed is off.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Valve_Fast) Examine If Closed asks: true when Valve_Fast is on.
    2. XIC(Valve_Closed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Valve_Closed is on.
  2. TON(T_ValveFb,1500,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_ValveFb toward 1500 ms (1.5 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

rungs.head: Rung 39
rungs.comment: THE REFILL BAND from the supply: the tank kept topped up, open under 85 %, sealed in to 90 %; the high-level switch, wired straight in, closes it whatever the transmitter says
rungs.words: When either (Silo_Level (Silo Level: Level transmitter, % of the volume (0-100)) is less than 85) or (Refill_Valve (Silo Refill: Refill valve on the inlet) is on), Silo_Level is less than 90, Silo_High (Silo HighLevel: High-level switch: 1 at its level and over) is off and EStop_OK (EStop OK: NC contact: 1 while healthy, 0 when pressed) is on, the rung turns Refill_Valve on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. LES(Silo_Level,85) Less Than asks: true when Silo_Level is less than 85.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Refill_Valve) Examine If Closed asks: true when Refill_Valve is on.
  2. LES(Silo_Level,90) Less Than asks: true when Silo_Level is less than 90.
  3. XIO(Silo_High) Examine If Open asks: true when Silo_High is off.
  4. XIC(EStop_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when EStop_OK is on.
  5. OTE(Refill_Valve) Output Energize does: turns Refill_Valve on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Refill_Valve on, and Refill_Valve’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.

rungs.head: Rung 43
rungs.comment: THE COUNT: one per container past the exit eye, on the leading edge
rungs.words: When Exit_PE (Exit_PE Detect: Detecting: a solid part is within range) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung makes Filled_Count (Containers counted out past the exit eye) = Filled_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Exit_PE) Examine If Closed asks: true when Exit_PE is on.
  2. ONS(Exit_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Exit_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. ADD(Filled_Count,1,Filled_Count) Add does: makes Filled_Count = Filled_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

    Path 1
    1. XIC(Line_VFD_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_VFD_Fault is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Line_VFD_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_VFD_Run is on.

rungs.comment: RESET clears the faults; one that is still there trips again

rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reset_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reset_PB_Pressed is on.
  2. A branch of 6 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Motor_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Motor_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Valve_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Valve_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Lance_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lance_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTU(Fill_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fill_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 5
    1. OTU(Format_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Format_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 6
    1. OTU(LT_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches LT_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Motor_Fault when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 56
rungs.comment: …a motor, valve or lance fault steady; a fill fault, a wrong container or a format the recipe does not know flashing
rungs.words: When either (Motor_Fault (The line's drive tripped (a motor overload) or is not ready) is on), (Valve_Fault (An outlet valve did not do what it was told) is on), (Lance_Fault (The lance did not move) is on), (Fill_Fault (A container did not fill in time) is on and Fl_Bit (The flasher bit) is on), (Format_Fault (The container on the scale weighs wrong for the format: the wrong container, or the wrong format set) is on and Fl_Bit is on) or (Format_OK (The format on the thumbwheel is 1 to 4) is off and Fl_Bit is on), the rung turns Lamp_Fault_On (Lamp_Fault On: Lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 6 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Motor_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Motor_Fault is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Valve_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Valve_Fault is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Lance_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lance_Fault is on.
    Path 4
    1. XIC(Fill_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_Fault is on.
    2. XIC(Fl_Bit) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fl_Bit is on.
    Path 5
    1. XIC(Format_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Format_Fault is on.
    2. XIC(Fl_Bit) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fl_Bit is on.
    Path 6
    1. XIO(Format_OK) Examine If Open asks: true when Format_OK is off.
    2. XIC(Fl_Bit) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fl_Bit is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault_On) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

Reg_Active.desc: A container is being registered: counting from the eye

Fill_Done.desc: The container under the lance is full; cleared when it leaves the prox

Tare_Taken.desc: The tare is in for the container on the scale

Fill_Req.desc: DEMAND mode: the FILL button pressed for the container under the lance

Fill_Fault.desc: A container did not fill in time

Valve_Fault.desc: An outlet valve did not do what it was told

Format_Fault.desc: The container on the scale weighs wrong for the format: the wrong container, or the wrong format set

Motor_Fault.desc: The line's drive tripped (a motor overload) or is not ready

LT_Fault.desc: The level transmitter disagrees with the high-level switch

Format.desc: Format_TW Value: The digits read as one number

Target.desc: Recipe: the net fill, tenths of a kg

Dribble.desc: Recipe: the last part of the fill on the dribble valve alone, tenths of a kg

Preact.desc: Recipe: what is still in the air when the dribble valve shuts, tenths of a kg

Slow_Cut.desc: Net weight where the dribble valve shuts: Target − Preact

Sys_OK.desc: The line may run: the E-Stop healthy and no fault latched

Start_PB_Pressed.desc: Start_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed

Run.desc: The conveyors are running (Start, sealed in until Stop, a fault, or one container done in ONE)

Stop_PB_Pressed.desc: Stop_PB Pressed: NC contact: 1 until pressed

Mode_Sel_Left.desc: Mode_Sel Left: 1 in the left position

Reg_ONS.desc: One-shot storage for the registration eye

Reg_Start.desc: The encoder count when the eye caught the container

Reg_Travel.desc: Pulses since the eye caught it

Creep.desc: Near the stop: the line at a quarter speed

Cont_Prox.desc: Cont_Prox Detect: Detecting: any solid part is within range

At_Fill.desc: A container is under the lance and has not been filled

Lance_Up.desc: Silo LanceUp: Fill lance up (retracted) switch

Valve_Closed.desc: Silo ValveClosed: Both outlet valves proved shut (their closed switches in series)

Line_VFD_SpeedRef.desc: Line_VFD SpeedRef: Speed reference: 0-10000 = 0-10.000 V = 0 to the 10 V frequency

T_Settle.desc: The scale settles after the container stops: 0.6 s

Weight.desc: Scale Weight: Weight on the scale, kg

Tare.desc: The empty container, weighed once it settles, tenths of a kg

Tare_OK.desc: The tare is in the format's window: the right container

Net.desc: What has gone into the container: Weight − Tare, tenths of a kg

Mode_Sel_Right.desc: Mode_Sel Right: 1 in the right position

Fill_PB_Pressed.desc: Fill_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed

Silo_Low.desc: The tank is low: under 10 %, until it is back over 20 %. No new fill starts

Fill_Go.desc: The fill is on for the container under the lance

Lance_Down.desc: Silo Lance: Fill lance air cylinder: down while on

T_LanceIn.desc: The lance's travel down into the container: 1.0 s

Valve_Fast.desc: Silo FillFast: Butterfly valve (bulk fill): open while on

Silo_Level.desc: Silo Level: Level transmitter, % of the volume (0-100)

Silo_High.desc: Silo HighLevel: High-level switch: 1 at its level and over

Exit_PE.desc: Exit_PE Detect: Detecting: a solid part is within range

Filled_Count.desc: Containers counted out past the exit eye
